steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Ah, Cleric Kal'tsit, you're finally here. Er, your mode of dress...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I was deeply honored by your invitation, but with sudden matters to attend to, the monastery could not prepare suitable evening attire for me. They found only this outfit buried in the storeroom. I hope you shan't mind.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Oh, quite naturally, I shan't. I'd go so far as to say your attire is utterly... utterly, formidably gallant.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Heidi, you don't just stand there. Here, this is Cleric Kal'tsit. Give her a greeting, and then hurry inside quickly.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Heidi?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Miss Heidi, it's good to meet you.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Ah—er—uh, th—um, I'm Heidi—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I know it already. An adorable name.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: —So you're—Cleric Kal'tsit, is that right? I often hear my uncle mention you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The pleasure is mine.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Cleric Kal'tsit, I imagine you know of Mr. Thomson too? Quite, this is Heidi Thomson before you, that strange fellow's daughter.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I see. Your father is a person worthy of respect.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Right, then, do come in, Cleric.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Thank you again for your generosity, Sir Vincent.

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: Oh, did you know the Count went to Londinium? Have you ever been in that city before?

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: Don't remind me! I once had everything packed up ready, and then! A Catastrophe Messenger came trotting along to say: the road ahead's blocked, you all go back.

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: I was beside myself returning home. Immediately had a great bout of illness.

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: Oh, my, how dearly wretched.

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Is that auspicious poet coming today? I've a few works I wrote in private, and I'd hoped he could do the honor of appraising them.

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: Perish the thought! Have you forgotten just how many manuscripts from 'thinkers' Thomson's torn up in front of the Count?

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: Oh, I remember. Thomson's ruthless. He even said himself, 'The clash of ideas ought to be a ruthless thing.' Truly frightening, he is.

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: It's not a be-all nor end-all to show off.

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: My, my, but the charm's all in young men like that, isn't it? Mettle to test, romantic and free.

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Of course I admit, I once admired Thomson for those qualities. But in front of the Count, Thomson still can't shake off his own deliberate arrogance.

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: Deliberate? Thomson?

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Isn't it obvious? He regards our esteemed Count, after all. Forget just nobility and status; in these last years, the Count's governed his land with perfect order. It's plain for all of us to see.

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: Hoh! Toron's not his land in name, mind, it's for all of us to manage, but I'll admit the Count deserves his reputation for leading! I do have to respect the man!

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: And lest we forget, he's had multiple invitations to the gatherings at Londinium. Don't you think our little place—allow me to admit our border situation—deserves some sense of pride?

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: Hah, nobles.

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: My, let's not make the topic so stiff. We're all people of Victoria, aren't we?

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Ha! People! Ever since that outrageous hanging, we can barely claim to know whose people we are!

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: Simmer down. We all regret Our Majesty's departure, but we can still drink a few toasts here today, you see?

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: In other words, today's a happy day. Don't bring up anything so frightful—look, here comes the Count.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: I overheard your conversation. Very intriguing, Richard. I'd much like to take a look at your writings.

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Oh, poppycock. Good Count, in comparison to you, my little effort pales like a man under a skyscraper.

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: That's right, Vincent, hurry and tell us of your trip to Londinium, let us all hear it. Who did you meet? Any Grand Dukes of living legend?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: In due time, everyone, in due time. The night has just begun. Don't forget, today is a day of festival celebration.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Allow me to introduce to you all two special guests of ours.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Cleric Kal'tsit, do come.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Good evening, honorable guests. Allow me to give my most sincere respects to you all.

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: What, now! By your appearance... my, you're a lady? Oh, what a mighty shame...

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: I think it's not much of a shame at all. Cleric Kal'tsit, good evening.

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Oh—oh—Cleric Kal'tsit, I believe I remember the Count speaking of you. I hear you treated his wife, and so garnered his good favor?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: With regards to the Count's wife, that was no light affair.

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: Do tell us about where you're from. Laterano clerics who aren't Sankta are so rare. My, let alone ones so... charming as you.

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: Beautiful miss, where do you come from? And where will you go?

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: Aren't I the one asking? Don't you interrupt.

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: The Count gives word that you're a pillar of talent. Do you have any inclination for philosophy or the arts? Any unique insights, perhaps?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You flatter me. It was only chance I aided the Count's wife. I have the distinction of his recognition, that's all.

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Oh—if you're familiar with the Count, surely you know Sir Thomson too, then?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Of course. Sir Thomson is a rarity of a scholar in Toron. I often hear the Count talk of him.

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Then things couldn't align better. Servant! Please fetch the wine I brought. I wish to have a proper causerie with the Count and the Cleric!

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: Don't you dominate our soirée, you egomaniac. Can't we all just chat about something fun? For example, that fashion walk at Londinium...

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: Fine by me. Everyone, just let me rest my legs for a while here. I'll be soaking in the knowledge.

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: Now, aren't you a lazy one. Your estate would be doubled by now if not for that!

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: Three wineries still isn't enough?

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: Oh, right, you mentioned you had another guest. I don't know if—

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Good evening, Misters and Misses.

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: Heidi! What are you doing here!

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Little Heidi, you're very prettily dressed today... that bastard Thomson. I fear for all my life, it's children alone where I'll never compare to him.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Now, now. Heidi isn't even of drinking age. None of you hand her a wine glass. Servants, if you could pour her a cream soda.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Don't always treat me like a child, Uncle Vincent.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: But drinking laws are drinking laws. Your father specifically warned me. After all, you're at that age...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: (Pout...)

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Alright, alright. Strike the cream soda and replace it with ginger ale.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I don't need you to coddle me like this!

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: Ha ha, little Heidi's eager to grow up.

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: It's sad. No father wants to see his daughter grow up this quickly. I was like that at her age too. Only wanted to buy some jewelry, and my father gave me a tongue-lashing for it.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Even if you won't let me drink, at least, can I join the dinner party? Let's see... I'll sit right here!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It would be my honor, Miss Heidi. Allow me to hold your hat for you.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Ah... no—no need, I'll be fine with it on...

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Good, then. Heidi, don't forget that you came here tonight in secret. In a while, you be good and sleep for the night upstairs.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Mnngh...

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: You dress very much like your mother, girl.

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: But right now—

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Mnnngh...!!

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Cleric Kal'tsit, do you think I'm still a child too?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: To you, I see no reason why it should matter.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Let me pour your glass for you. Here's your ginger ale.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Th... thank you...

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Is it to your liking?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: It's actually quite a nice drink.

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: Oh, my, there is no alcohol in ginger ale, is there? What's gotten your face red?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: The girl's wary of strangers. It's nothing new.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Come, friends! Seeing as we're all present, let us officially begin!

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: You're most correct! The height of Leithanien's arts capture all hearts alike, but those Leithanians are far too pompous about themselves! What affords them to look down on us!

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: Leithanien, oh, Leithanien. They've had too much misfortune... I haven't stopped hearing Witch King stories since I was a baby. Who knows if the Twin Empresses will have managed to sort out that king by the time I visit the place!

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: Who would visit knowing the terror of the Witch King...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Unlike the monarchs who ascended young, the Witch King became emperor at nearly fifty years of age, and then governed Leithanien for many more.

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Undoubtedly, the Witch King is the greatest Caster in all our lands. He turned himself into a freak of nature!

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: He's just like those horrible stories depicted him. His horns all bent into strange shapes, emitting this strange energy...

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: Oh! I've never seen the Witch King shown in a newspaper before—*belch*—Sorry there, this wine's just too fine. But I have seen photos of the Twin Empresses, come to think of it. One gleaming gold, one dark as night.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Leithanien is in flux. Presumably, the Witch King rarely leaves his tower. From start to finish, he's gazed dispassionately at Leithanien, and even when he grants an audience, it's as he casts a grand shadow from atop his tower.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Yet the last time he touched the ground, he was morphed beyond recognition. His wretchedness, his two horns cut off by the Twin Empresses apiece, drew true sighs of lament.

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: The full picture of that coup d'etat is still unclear to us, but to my knowledge, even our most heroically adored Wanderer would never match the Witch King's true strength.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This being why when the Empresses' Voice arrived at Victoria escorted by the knights, the Grand Dukes were all still willing to suspend their quarrels, and treat each other with respect.

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Pardon? It sounds as though—you've been to Londinium before?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I arrived from there. It was a local Sankta's enlightening me that led me on this path.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Ha-ha, Kal'tsit, didn't I say? These are all wonderful friends of mine. See just how popular you are.

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: Truth is, I have a girl about the same age as you. She only knows how to splash my hard-earned money away all the damned day... How nice it'd be if she could learn from you.

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: Getting to know you tonight has been a truly wonderful time. Can I ask if you're still single, dear Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Cleric Kal'tsit!

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Oh, Heidi, don't cut in so randomly. You should be heading upstairs to turn in about now.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Allow her to speak, Count. In this day and age, children are always much more mature than we imagine.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Hm.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Cleric Kal'tsit... have—can I ask if you've been to Ursus before?

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Oh, that nation rife with rebellion and violence.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: When I was studying abroad, I spent some time at Deity Grypherburg. Are you interested in Ursus?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Yes!

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Papa once gave me a few books to read, by an Ursus author...

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Ursus only ever produces two kinds of arts: raucous sensationalism, or true eternal greats.

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: If Thomson liked it, chances are it was the latter, wasn't it?

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Hmph. You lot really do trust him.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Papa really put him in high esteem. He even wanted to go to Deity Grypherburg himself to visit him, but business always meant he had to put it off, and this year with his old injuries flaring up again, he wasn't able to go.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your father was injured?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: That's right. He broke his knee, and then put off surgery for too long, so it's not fully treated.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: I warned him. Ah, no idea what happened last year. He came scrabbling back with wounds all over, and all he'd say was he ran into a robber and dropped off a cliff. Wasn't interested in saying much else.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Do you want to go to Ursus? Miss Heidi?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Now that won't do! The death of the last Emperor and the rebellions had a profound effect on the country. Should you want to study there, you'd do well to wait a few years first.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I'm just talking about it... What impression do you have of the country?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'll tell you a story.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's the story of how Ursus's Sixth Army were annihilated, without a trace, by a bottle of vodka.

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Well, this rumor doesn't sound plausible at all.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: When any event is boiled down to its cause, its conclusion tends to sound unexpected. We're all used to the process, aren't we?

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: That does make sense.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It began with a ruffian from the Army 'collecting rent' in one of their garrison regions, and without realizing, he menaced a noble.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That act fermented the whole way through. The Sixth Army then were always considered utterly corrupt, the old nobles' power rooted too deep, while the Fifth Army were unconditionally obedient to the young Emperor and the brand new State Council.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We have no way to know for sure who fired the first shot, but as for the outcome, the Fifth Army ultimately seized the chance to revolt, and in between two cities' paths, started a direct firefight with the Sixth Army.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: The prologue to 'The Great Rebellion' comes in many editions. I've definitely heard a few things of the Sixth Army's varied deeds.

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: They fought just like that?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If it were that simple, then it wouldn't have been dubbed 'The Great Rebellion.'

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Being a border guard outfit, the Fourth Army, with a domain of authority and influence decidedly not in the hinterlands, suddenly switched sides to support the State Council, and proactively declared no relationship to the 'traitors' in the Sixth Army.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: After the execution of a few prepared scapegoats, the old nobility had only the Sixth and Eighth Armies left in hand.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Come winter the following year, the nobility backing the Eighth Army pulled that same trick, capitulating alike to the Emperor.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And so, the bitter fate of the Sixth Army who had staked it all on one throw, we can well imagine.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And the cause of all of this—very simple, one we all know. Simply a drunk ruffian, taking the vodka bottle he had in hand to attack a young noble.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: A marvelous story, Cleric Kal'tsit, and might I even confirm, this tale is little removed from the reality at all.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Heidi, I would not tell you that 'this is how Ursus is.' Every civilization in this world deserves you seeing it for yourself. They should be appreciated, and have to be reflected upon.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In that Ursus you admire, what have you seen?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Perhaps the farms and public houses, perhaps the grand heroes, perhaps the highs and lows of life in Deity Grypherburg's opera house. But what I've seen is the Great Rebellion's aftermath, an age on the verge of collapse.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Might Victoria have such an age of its own someday?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I will not guarantee it either way, Miss Heidi.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: How could it! Here, you little child. Are you afraid now, because of Cleric Kal'tsit's smidgen story of Ursus?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: I've no intent to insult the Ursus people, but the Empire of Ursus is unarguably a savage, unreasonable nation.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: But right now, isn't Londinium just as—

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: —Don't even say it. Though it pains us all that it happened, did Victoria waver for even a moment?

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: Alright, alright, Count, seeing as the topic's come around, I think it's high time you told us about that trip to Londinium, yes? That's what we're most interested in.

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: What high nobility did you meet?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: I'd be honored to tell. Truth is, on the way, the Duke of Normandy personally invited me to a shindig, together at his flagship...

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: What! And you managed to keep from telling us all the way to today...!

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: My, it was the Duke of Normandy himself... He always did detest Leithanians. Did he and the envoys of the Empresses' Voice have a scuffle?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: No, but by his retainer's words, the good Duke never once made eye contact with those gorgeous envoys that evening.

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Ah-ha, now that's the proper manner of a 'Duke.'

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Ursus's theatrical Grand Dukes might number more in hundreds than tens—alright, maybe not that many, but they are quite unchecked, and if I might add, somewhat incompetent too.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: That's a form of arrogance, but I must say, everyone who's experienced the Londinium manner for themselves would echo the sentiment.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: I trust the Duke of Normandy need only rely on his own power to make those Leithanian greed-blinded extremists know their place for a few dozen years. Let alone the fact we've certainly more than a single Duke...

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Tuckered out, Heidi?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Hm? No... I'm still thinking about what Cleric Kal'tsit said. Could I talk with her alone for a bit?

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: Oh, if we're to talk Londinium without Kal'tsit, it would certainly be much duller.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You flatter me.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Now, no rush. I see the Baron of Rye is calling at me, so I'll need to chit-chat with him now. I assure you, I'll be back shortly to tell the full tale.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Does this all bore you? Miss Heidi?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Huh? Ah... no, it doesn't, I'm alright.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Fine... erm, it's just, I thought we'd talk more about poetry, or the wheat harvest, but it turns out not...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Sick of foreign politics?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Um, ha ha...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's what tonight's dinner party was meant for.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I can see, you also consider it somewhat boring, don't you?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: You understand more than anyone, and you can't stand all those people in a giggling gaggle around Uncle Vincent, correct?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You seem to have some misunderstanding about me...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Ha ha, we only met tonight, didn't we? You're right, Cleric Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You can call me just Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Then, Kal'tsit... could you walk with me?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: In a while longer, Uncle Vincent will have me sent off into the loft. I certainly don't want to go to bed this early.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: The snow seems to have gotten heavier. Would you mind that...?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: —I wouldn't. Allow me to accompany you.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: What a snowstorm!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The biggest one in recent years.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I like the snow, Kal'tsit, and I like my home too.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Phew... how cold.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Everyone's all huddling inside by the fireplace.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: It's just us two now, Kal'tsit... hee-hee, Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: —It's so difficult to be alone with you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You're yet young... Heidi.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your father shouldn't have let you get involved so easily.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: But that's what I wanted, Kal'tsit. I wished to do something or other, instead of hiding in the warm house, gazing out, just as a child would.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: When winter truly comes, would a single oak of Victoria's be spared from the blizzard? Then that being the case, we should prepare early.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You resemble your father greatly.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: —Is that a compliment?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Let's say it is.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Hee-hee... ah, nobody should find us here, so...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Now I can hand these letters to you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your father's intelligence operatives are never late. They're the best Messengers, workers, and aspirants in all of Victoria—except this time.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Has something happened?
The young Heidi makes not an innocent step more.
She is right. Before upheaval arrives, the young must always be the soonest to prepare.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: —There are two letters, Dame Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: One from all of Victoria, and another from 'Kazdel.'
